prompt: A student has taken $5$ tests with an average score of $82$. What score is needed on a sixth test to raise the average to exactly $84$?
explanation: The key identity is sum $=$ mean $\times$ count.
Current sum: $5 \times 82 = 410$. Required sum for six tests averaging $84$: $6 \times 84 = 504$.
The sixth score must make up the difference: $504 - 410 = 94$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in terms of the deficit
steps: To lift the average by $2$ points, all five existing tests need $2$ extra points each — a deficit of $10$.
The new test must also hit the target of $84$ itself, plus cover that $10$.
$84 + 10 = 94$. This "cover the deficit" view is fast and makes the answer feel inevitable.
